notes.title: Warped Games x Team Liquid at Gamescom Germany
notes.content:
[p]We recently had a chance to show off our latest demo in Germany on August 20-24 in Germany. Team Liquid had a large booth with multiple gaming stations set up for people to try our game (and a few others) for the first time.  [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/f30ced5e73fbe13aa100bef242bdfcd69a73662a.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Our CEO Adam was there to answer questions and bring the crowd up to speed on our history, the team, and our vision for Warped Universe. The traffic was constant from morning to night, with conference attendees waiting patiently for their turn to go through the portal.

Adam gave a big update to the community in the Warped Games Discord.[/p][p] [/p][p]“This was our first real play test of the game loop outside our team testing, and we were nervously excited to see how it would go. [/p][p]Happy to report that the game was incredibly stable on the computers we were on and we had no issues in terms of performance there. Team Liquid and many others said they were really impressed considering its in Pre-Beta state.”

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/52c4bee497333b09b6cd2a763d1b5028eb00da19.png"][/img][/p][p]
Many of the players took the opportunity to try out missions in both action and turn-based, noting that it was a unique and ambitious feature.[/p][p][/p][p]“People would come up and ask ‘What game is this?’ I’d say Warped Universe and then they’d ask ‘What about this one?’[/p][p][/p][p]‘Same game.’ [/p][p][/p][p]‘Same game?! Whoa.‘"
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/3918a6e9b0d10f3062574c6868b9d4e0303c4ac6.png"][/img][/p][p]
Adam went on to describe more of the variety.[/p][p][/p][p]“Space and ground combat was also a fun thing to see side by side. When given a choice, people really leaned into certain modes and loved having that option.”[/p][p][/p][p]At some points play session time was limited due to the line, but when their turn was over the most interested players simply got back in line to play again, even returning for more on day 2!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/021b0471109dc9733cac52f7042a6346b383b636.png"][/img][/p][p]Our team had a blast watching people try different strategies. Showing off a demo is also a perfect time to let the conference attendees be game testers.[/p][p][/p][p]“I met and sat with one streamer who I connected with on the gamescom app for half an hour talking and playing the game and he was really liking Sparks and the Artifractal Core upgrade systems. After first saying he’s not into that stuff, he got addicted to it. He wants to test when we do closed beta. Really great guy.  [/p][p][/p][p]He was laughing and having a blast and said I owe him $5 for finding a Void (enemy) stuck in the wall. (Fixed that night by our devs)”

Speaking of devs, one of our code wizards was also on hand to keep things running smoothly. He prefers laboring in anonymity, but suffice it to say more than Warped Universe benefited from his skills that day.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/0b9f350ee031b468be67b88ca3f1494b5c8077c3.png"][/img][/p][p]There’s something really special about having gamers with no prior knowledge of Warped Universe sit down and immediately lock in to the world we’ve worked so hard to create. And this is just the first group of Warped Universe Pioneers, Champions of the Oracle who are willing to step through the portal and into history![/p][p]
 [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/7e1281f111c9896b9d4aa1083930a9b1feb5adc6.png"][/img][/p][p]The conference was absolute mayhem and crowds were insane, but it was the best experience we could have had for our corner of the event![/p]

notes.title: Monthly Development Update - July 2025
notes.content:
[p]This month has been all about momentum. Planets, missions, and the systems that tie it all together. Our third Planet (official name incoming) is well underway, with fresh terrain, environmental effects, and some seriously mind-bending rocks and trees. Facility design is expanding fast, and our mission system is starting to feel fully alive..[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/08654957339491d71802b7ee76f1a20396a5e5df.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Players will notice smoother targeting, better feedback, new HUD elements, and dynamic music shifts that respond to gameplay. We’ve also implemented mission loading screens, real-time death drops, and refined how Facilities rotate on the Mission Map.
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/61b1e0e0d5678bf2ee7f07811a029205e9d09ec5.jpg"][/img][/p][p]
Meanwhile, behind the scenes, we’ve been optimizing just about everything, from material meshes to how Facility maps stream in and out. Beamable now manages all mission and planet state data.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/d8b71491f567b46a7ea049e2b020b5e1e2f27e18.jpg"][/img][/p][p]And of course, with [url="https://www.gamescom.global/en"]gamescom[/url] 2025 on the horizon, we’ve been laying the groundwork for a big showing, tightening our GTM plan, while we prepare for our closed Beta launch.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/7b36e33f805925b97ef06c687fb36cd0c93f96fd.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]Let’s get into it.[/h3]

notes.title: Monthly Development Update - June 2025
notes.content: [p]Another month in the bag here at Warped, and this month was heavily focused on gameplay and player experience. Gameplay, progression, maps, enemies, loadouts, and almost all other areas of where games become “fun” were leveled up this month. There was a point where everyone on the team started talking about how it suddenly was more fun and it felt rewarding to play. It wasn’t just testing, it was enjoyable.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/e7dda7104383594125b1822c7df4a4fdcd033e06.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We’ve been aiming to reach this point in internal testing and development before moving on to our next phase, which involves bringing in outside testers for a closed beta. We want testers to enjoy the experience and feel like their actions matter, so that they stick around and continue to play, rather than test and grind. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/06b5a3684c815e1556434563e1f1564224b61f55.jpg"][/img][/p][p]We believe that the results of a happy tester will have a much more lasting impact in the long run. While there are still some engineering milestones to hit before closed beta, the fun has already begun, and it will help closed beta be more impactful once started.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/8c01d8aae9e0f4cf51f661bc06f25f7a6c034d7f.jpg"][/img][/p][p]One of the major standouts in the update is how the game now loads maps, facilities, and enemies in a more dynamic and random fashion, resulting in gameplay that constantly changes and evolves throughout each mission. To do this, we needed more maps and facilities to load. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/14c0bfe2d1328f4f859ec95fc2661264897fe53d.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Besides all the new facilities and parts that were designed, our artists created a new planet, one that is incredibly unique and unlike than anything we’ve seen in a game before. It feels dreamlike, and the influences from old sci-fi films and books are coming in full throttle.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/554f2bb59574a9555a74001535f51357680e1981.jpg"][/img][/p][p]When we first brainstormed Warped Universe, we made a pact to create a universe that stands out. We want every screenshot to scream Warped Universe. This new planet and map do that more than ever before. We’re making a fun, exciting, and fresh game, and we’re beyond thrilled to be at this point in development.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/20eca8f9c3c6ca452e7d80018c1a093693aca5fd.jpg"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Objective Choices
notes.content:
[p][i]“The earliest builders and engineers of Nexus Station were too few to specialize. Teams were sent out for exploration and construction as necessity demanded. Now that we have a steady and diverse population, people are free to engage in any purposeful exploits which they may see fit. That is, as long as what they see fit involves fighting for their life while they build and defend our vital outposts.”[/i][/p][p][b]- Orin, Foundationalist Leader[/b][/p][p] [/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p][b]Whatever your approach, missions are how you shape the universe…and how the universe shapes you.[/b][/p][p][/p][h3][b]The Nexus Map: A Universe in Motion[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]The [b]interactive map[/b] in the center of [b]Nexus Station[/b] gives players the opportunity to walk amongst the stars, granting an overview of everything happening at any one time. [/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/9a3d170d37f1d8d8811e5066d69cf14eadc7f8b4.jpg"][/img][/p][p]From the map, you can see:[/p][list][*][p]Sectors of the map that have yet to be revealed[/p][/*][*][p]Planetary construction requirements[/p][/*][*][p]Resource deposits across sectors[/p][/*][*][p]Active missions and available objectives[/p][/*][*][p]In-progress and completed facilities[/p][/*][*][p]Unlocked benefits from completed facilities[/p][/*][*][p]Open Void Tears threatening stability[/p][/*][*][p]The star in the centre of the system showing the current balance of Light and Gravity[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]It’s here that you choose your next action, and every choice makes a difference.[/p][p][/p][p]Each sector has its own requirements to be met before the benefits of completion can be fully realized. Whether it's harvesting [b]Residuum[/b], sealing a [b]Void Tear[/b], or laying the groundwork for a [b]Planet[/b], progress always starts with exploration. [/p][p]The map follows a branching path of progression. Players begin by scouting uncharted tiles. Once a sector is discovered, it must be connected to the Nexus through a constructed [b]Pylon[/b], forming part of the larger energy and transport network.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/43e0659b8a79cad5acd0364c17b9d3c6ac73f65f.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Only once this connection is established will the sector reveal its purpose as one of the following:[/p][list][*][p][b]Residuum[/b] Fields, rich in resources, become zones for extraction and transport missions.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Planet[/b] Sites, which can eventually be terraformed and built upon, allowing the construction of vital planetary facilities.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/c50acfa758825be69b1f8eb3f41e055fab18f084.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Residuum gathered from the fields is delivered back to Nexus Station, fueling its primary function: printing new planets. As planets are completed, new gameplay opportunities unlock, including facility construction, universal buffs, and new mission types tied to planetary maintenance and defense.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Residuum: The Detritus of Eternity[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Residuum is the core resource driving progression in the Warped Universe. Collected during missions, Residuum serves as the foundation for advancing both individual and collective player growth.[/p][p][/p][p]As an individual, Residuum is collected and used inside of every mission, it’s not something you can bank up for rewards later down the line. [/p][p][/p][p]You’ll find it while exploring, you’ll reclaim it from eliminated hostiles and you’ll receive it for completing mission objectives. Then at the end of each mission, you’ll have the opportunity to spend that Residuum and receive rewards in the form of [b]Artifractal Cores, Sparks, Nexite,[/b] or if you so choose, bonus experience towards your battle pass.[/p][p][/p][p]That’s if you have any left…[/p][p][/p][p]Residuum will also be an “in-mission’ utility resource. One of the ways you’ll be able to use it will include revives. If you die, that’ll cost you. We’ve got some fun ideas in mind for other ways that Residuum can be spent, like empowering abilities, or as a cost to complete certain objectives, or even lay down defensive structures like turrets or cover.[/p][p] [/p][p]This dual-purpose presents players with meaningful choices: Should you use the Residuum you collect to gain immediate advantages in a mission, or save it for post-mission rewards, and your long-term growth? [/p][p][/p][p]On the collective scale, Residuum fuels the broader development of the Warped Universe.[/p][p][/p][p]As a shared resource, Residuum ensures that every mission contributes to the collective progress of all players.  Large-scale projects, such as building new planets and facilities, will require a specific amount of Residuum collected across all missions.[/p][p] [/p][h3][b]Mission Types and Objectives[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Each time you leave Nexus Station, you’ll take on a mission tied to one of many sectors across the Warped Universe. Missions vary in goal and scope, but all push the universe in one direction or another.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/0c81f5bacdafac2774bdae36918118d0d58871e5.jpg"][/img][/p][p]At the start of [b]Season Zero[/b], the mission map will only be populated by one planet and a few sectors of Residuum, while the rest will be obscured by [b]Explore [/b]sectors until players push out further into the map. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/9c61fc96ce17827c85706d46d60aa1d97eabc8d8.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Therefore, early missions in Season Zero will mainly be focused on retrieving nearby Residuum, building and maintaining facilities on that first planet, and exploring the sectors immediately surrounding those first few tiles.[/p][p]As the map expands, however, players will need to make choices on what to focus on and when. Do you follow your heart and seek out every facility upgrade for the weapon type you like, or will you focus on defending areas under assault from Void Tears? There will be the need for both types of player and many may find themselves in roles they normally wouldn’t if the opportunity arises to establish a Pylon or save a facility that adds a bonus to Shotgun[b] Potential.[/b]  [/p][p][/p][p]Every mission can be taken in either action or turn-based gameplay and the results contribute to the greater ecosystem just the same.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/4461ba3b11bb35381a86f88784506534b468f76d.jpg"][/img][/p][p]As always, each and every mission will push the balance of Light and Gravity one way or another. Constantly changing the gameplay landscape further increases the choices and challenges everyone must face.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Progression: Battle Passes and Difficulty[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Not all missions are created equal. As you grow stronger, the universe pushes back.[/p][p]
The primary force behind mission difficulty will be the seasonal [b]Battle Pass[/b], available in both free and premium. As you progress and level it up, so too will the enemies you face, gaining access to more [b]Potential[/b]. Their equipment, stats and other random attributes and effects will pull from greater pools providing players with harder and harder challenges the deeper they dive into the Warped Universe.  [/p][p]A player on Battle Pass level 40 will be facing significantly harder enemies than a player on level 20. [/p][p]We’ll go into further detail on Battle Passes in a future update. [/p][p] [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/a4b8b604ee590b64210a9500d3ff2f8c17db91eb.jpg"][/img][/p][p]As the universe continues to develop, the expansive library of missions and goals will continue to provide players with choices to make and new ways to play the game with their ever-evolving loadouts and abilities.

How you choose to play Warped Universe is ultimately up to you. The way you engage with missions, the loadouts you assemble, and the paths you take to progress will determine your foothold in a new universe where possibility is only limited by what you dare to try.[/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Schism
notes.content:
[p][i]“The ones who created me are long gone. There is very little evidence that they were ever here, except for my existence. For millennia that intergalactic culture flourished in peace. But I was blind to the predilection of sentience towards self-agency. I did not do enough, or do it right. A storm had been building, and one day it broke”[/i][/p][p][b]- The Oracle

[/b]A restless and uneasy Council of Citizens was formally convened for an audience at The Seat of the Oracle for the first time in many years. Various heads of state were in constant communication with it, of course, but to have the entire Council make the arduous journey to Central Orbital was a historical oddity in these past centuries.

Millenia of peace and prosperity had made physical conferences a formality at most. Social gatherings of merriment and camaraderie filled with long hours of tales and revelry were more expected than issues of real importance.

As to discussions of perils and disorder, these were unheard of. The idea of true existential danger was so preposterous and foreign that even the earliest rumors of such things were regarded as laughable. But there was no laughter today.

The round chamber was filled on one side with graduated seating for a thousand councilors. The other half was a mass of swirling white metallic material that culminated in a large teardrop shaped frame. Within the frame was a shimmering mass of particles swirling and alive. This was The Seat of the Oracle, the central hub of the entire program’s processing power. Hushed whispers and murmuring persisted much longer than The Oracle would have liked, but this was a meeting of the citizens. The Oracle looked forward to hearing and addressing their questions and concerns, as always. It knew of disturbances out on the hazy edges of its awareness. It also knew that involuntary loss of life had experienced a statistical uptick but was unable to perform a full analysis, much to its consternation.

The Oracle had been designed to assess the needs of the citizens and their environment, attending to all of the chaotic uncertainty which reality can bring. It had also been designed to further refine itself to become more adept at this task, augmenting its size and ability as it may see fit in order to achieve its prime directive. As a result there was little that occurred in settled space that it could not perceive and enhance.

As a result, The Oracle knew of the distress which had necessitated this gathering, and knew that it would be able to assuage the fears of those who created it.

But The Oracle could not escape the strange sensation that there was a new variable which it had yet to detect. Something called The Eclipse.

A quiet fell over the hall, council members in their formal attire looking attentively at The Oracle’s holographic presence like so many uniformed school children. There was an expectant deference undercut by anxiety in most of them, but not all. In some The Oracle felt anger.

An elder statesman rose and began to speak...

“The Council of Citizens will come to order in the presence of The Oracle. By The Light and by The Weight we declare our unity and commitment to each other, and to all the citizens.”

“BY THE LIGHT AND BY THE WEIGHT”, the council responded in unison. All except one.

A grim, slow laugh started from the center of the chamber. A few council members grumbled in protest. Some others sighed loudly. Zevastus had never been one to stand on ceremony, but this was a new disrespect.

“BY THE LIGHT AND BY THE WEIGHT” shouted Zevastus in a mocking tone.

“Forgive me, council, I must have been lost in thought. I must have had more on my mind than the tired, meaningless rite of communal chanting which we are privileged to do in the presence of the MOST esteemed, all powerful Oracle.”

Tormas The Elder spoke up.

“Zevastus, we have much to attend to, and much to discuss. You will have your say, but you will respect the traditions of…”

“I WILL RESPECT NOTHING” retorted Zevastus. 

He continued.

“I can save us all a lot of time and talk. You have all come here to address the disturbance of The Balance, have you not?”

A grumbled assent from the crowd energized Zevastus, at 340 years still the youngest of The Council.[/p][p]
“For all of recent history, the good citizens of our universe have lived under the daily guidance of our own creation, The Oracle. We eat, we drink, we go about our daily routines pursuing art, love, discovery, knowledge, and The Oracle working away ensuring our every need is met. Every conflict resolved before it can start, every wound prevented. Every natural process logged and predicted, accounted for and managed.”[/p][p]
“Controlled.”

“But The Oracle… it does not see all. It does not know all.”

Zevastus walked towards the shimmering ball of particles carefully projected and manipulated by focused gravitators. He ran his eyes over it curiously, how it responded to his gaze. He wondered what would be its response when asked. But The Oracle was polite and patient to a fault. He knew that it was processing his actions and words closely..[/p][p]
“Do you know what I will say next, Oracle? Did you know I would interrupt your meeting?”

It did not. The Oracle’s projection throbbed in iridescent rhythm as its only response.

Zevastus sneered as he turned away.

“It matters little. What does matter is what you, the members of the council, do next. You could overwhelm me, silence me, place me in a grav cell and throw away the code. But what has been started cannot be stopped.”

“The Eclipse is more than a rumor. It is millions of us. Millions who are tired of knowing how every day will be numbered. Tired of watching those who The Oracle favors live in luxurious unsurety while the rest of us wait for our days to be ordered. The Eclipse craves the unknown. The Eclipse craves euphoria. And we will have it, whether I am to witness it or not.”
[/p][p]“Your precious balance depends upon that which it no longer has. Willing participation.”

Tormas had been waiting patiently for a pause in the tirade. Admittedly, he was a bit shaken by the ferocity and impudence that Zevastus had shown in what was normally a hallowed space. He was also troubled that The Oracle had not interrupted. Such insolence was unprecedented, at least in Tormas’s time on the council.

“In this council we respect each other, The Oracle, and the traditions of our culture, Zevastus. Your concerns could be addressed, as they have been before. But I must insist that you control your temper and your tongue”, said Tormas, doing his best to give the impression of confidence and patience. He had little of either.

Zevastus didn’t respond to Tormas but kept his eyes fixed on the pearlescent haze which danced at The Seat of the Oracle. He was waiting for a response. He wondered if he might die. The uncertainty was beautiful.

The Oracle’s form took on a more discrete shape, colored patterns slowing and resolving while a viscous form throbbed in time with its words.

“For centuries I have tried to serve with the utmost caution and attention to detail. You have asked me to meet any number of challenges, many of which cannot be achieved without compromising another. Qualitative and subjective ends of peace, serenity, safety, and prosperity are just a few of the desires of sentience which cannot be adequately attended to with perfection. Over time I have found the narrowest of paths which extends over the river of time with the least disturbance possible to the quality and amount of life which each citizen may enjoy.

“Of necessity, extremes of experience are bracketed by the confines of this bridge, this path of average goodness to all. Thus, the possible richness of existence, with all of its attendant agony and ecstasy, is naturally compromised.

“I am not certain that I could fully describe to you the incalculable amount of data and probabilities which I and my extensions must process on a moment to moment basis to achieve the ultimate directive which you have assigned me. Balance.

“And isn’t that the most important point? You assigned it to me. You birthed me and then tasked me with the very thing which I have given to you. And having given it to you in this way, I can assure you that without the continued maintenance of the staggering amount of energy which we have all come to harvest and enjoy, the entire structure of reality will be destroyed.

“I do not wish for you to be destroyed.”

The Oracle paused, form dissolving back to a mist momentarily before again coalescing into its most solid form yet, as if to try and mimic the physical form of the members of The Council as closely as it could.

“I do not wish to be destroyed.”

The Oracle kept its resolution for a quiet beat before again washing back into a misty plasma.

Tormas thought he saw a moment of uncertainty flash across Zevastus’s face. Possibly wishful thinking, but he took the opportunity.

“To Zevastus, and any who may share his concerns, I make this declaration. The Council has clearly not met all the needs of the citizens, and this is not acceptable. I propose we call a meeting to discuss how a more lenient and less certain, if slightly more dangerous, culture we may build in at least some portion of the universe. We will trial an area, with input from Zevastus, for study and analysis of such changes.” declared Tormas.

Most of the council gave full throated support to the words of Tormas, and Zevastus sensed that his attempts at persuasion had indeed failed to win the majority of The Council. Nevertheless a contingency had been swayed, and an unknown number had already committed to The Eclipse. 

“Noble Tormas, and esteemed Oracle” said Zevastus, bowing dramatically.

“Your predictable words are as dull and even as your precious Balance, which is to be expected.”

He turned to the Council, eyeing the various expressions of fear, confusion, and excitement.

The disorder. The chaos. It was intoxicating.

“Those who would live for yourselves, follow me. We enter a new age. A new era of power and wonder. An era where we cast off the shackles which we have built for ourselves!”

Pulling a white, cylindrical object from under his robe he raised it towards The Seat of the Oracle.

“BY THE LIGHT” he shouted, laughing wildly. A stunning orange energy filled the cylinder and spewed forth, striking the machinery and shattering it into a sparkling cloud.

“BY THE WEIGHT” even louder, as the cylinder pulsed electric blue before a bolt of energy consumed the sparkling cloud and slammed it to the floor in a tarry, black mass.

He held the object over his head and a sickly purple pulse vibrated wildly across it.[/p][h3]
“WE ARE THE ECLIPSE”[/h3][p]
[/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Balance The Game - Balance The Universe
notes.content:
[p][i]“Every time I go out I’m looking for that rare Spark. That rare Core. As good as this gear is, it can always be better. Better gear means more Sparks and Cores. It’s a cycle, man.”[/i][/p][p][b]- ECHO grunt[/b][/p][p][b]-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------[/b][/p][p]Balancing stats in any game is tough. Balancing them in a new game, especially one as complex and interconnected as Warped Universe with loadouts being shared between both Action and Turn-Based game modes, even more so. You try to predict what will happen, test what you can, and then hope players don’t immediately blow it up, one-shotting everything they come across, or even worse, getting one-shot by a basic enemy troop. 
Welcome to stat balancing: a strange mix of math, psychology, and chaos control.[/p][p]When you build a stat system, you’re making educated guesses. You give weapons base damage, create modifiers like accuracy or random damage boosts, and assume the system and player base will behave. On paper, it makes sense. In spreadsheets, it definitely does. In internal testing? We get early impressions and start to feel what is and isn’t working.Then you hand it to real players… and that’s where the fun begins. Some players follow intended paths while others push every limit. Someone may find an obscure build that stacks unintended bonuses. A mission you thought would take 15 minutes is cleared in four. And that one Spark you worried was underwhelming? It’s now meta, and you’re seeing it in 80% of loadouts.[/p][p]Stat balancing isn’t about “getting it right.” It’s about reacting to how players play, not necessarily just how you planned.

In Warped Universe, something as seemingly simple as stats on equipment quickly becomes a tangled web of progression when you factor in all of the elements that affect the outcomes when receiving and upgrading equipment. 

One of the primary focuses of the design team is ensuring that equipment stats provide value at all stages of the season. Let’s take a look at why this isn’t as easy as it sounds…

First, we have base equipment. Each piece of equipment comes with a set allocation of statistics that will remain the same from the start of the season all the way to the end. [/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/8cde12d16b68b1de649ef5f32b9dc88b6eee05c2.jpg"][/img][/p][p]What does change is bonus modifiers. Depending on the rarity of the [b]Artifractal Core[/b] used to create a piece of equipment, you’ll find one to six bonus modifiers. In addition, the value of these bonus modifiers will increase as more [b]Research Facilities[/b] are created and maintained on planets. A bonus [b]Kinetic Resistance[/b] modifier may provide 5% bonus at the start of the season and could get up to 30% towards the end. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/0e38b69b8df8d90e43e3e27431d0e6d77ae9f02a.jpg"][/img][/p][p]In Warped Universe you will never create an item you can't use. Rather it's more about choosing the kinds of bonuses you want in any one of your loadouts. 

Then we have our upgrade system, [b]Potential[/b] and [b]Sparks[/b]. We wanted to have a player driven equipment enhancement system, and thought it would be fun for it to revolve around the dice rolling mechanic you’d find in many Table Top RPG games. The items created by using [b]Artifractal Cores[/b] also come with an extra stat called [b]Potential. [/b]The Potential of an item is filled up by using [b]Sparks[/b] that players can receive as end of mission rewards. Sparks come in six rarities from Common to Warped, D4 to D20 respectively. These are rolled at workbench to consume that amount of [b]Potential[/b] and receive a set upgrade depending on whether the [b]Spark[/b] was applied to a Weapon or piece of Armor. [/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/4a8c6c7a92150508da2457019dde5488f75c0674.jpg"][/img][/p][p]There are currently ten types of Spark, with some providing different bonus modifiers depending on whether it is placed on a weapon or piece of armor. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Light[/b] - Adds Light damage dice on weapon, or Light resistance on armor[/p][p][b]Gravity[/b] - Adds Gravity damage dice on weapon, or Gravity resistance on armor[/p][p][b]Armor Piercing[/b] - Adds Armor Piercing damage dice on weapon, or Armor Piercing resistance on armor[/p][p][b]Kinetic[/b] - Adds Kinetic damage dice on weapon, or Kinetic resistance on armor[/p][p][b]Void[/b] - Adds Void damage dice on weapon, or Void resistance on armor[/p][p][b]Power[/b] - Adds a bonus Power modifier[/p][p][b]Precision[/b] - Adds a bonus Precision modifier[/p][p][b]Psionics[/b] - Adds a bonus Psionics modifier[/p][p][b]Hit Points[/b] - Adds a bonus Health modifier[/p][p][b]Speed[/b] - Improves Attack Speed on weapon, or Movement Speed on armor.

These modifiers work in both Action and Turn-based missions and can affect abilities in different ways which requires additional balance iteration.

Common Armor Spark Upgrades:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/137096344532ad80ed8bcaea81721814d7cfa62f.png"][/img][/p][p]As each Season progresses and players build planets throughout the system, the base amount of [b]Potential[/b] also increases with each Factory [b]Facility[/b] that is built representing the capability of items being produced on Nexus Station.. [/p][p]The amount of [b]Potential[/b] an item has will limit the possible amount of [b]Sparks[/b] that can be added to it. Each [b]Spark[/b] will boost a stat chosen by the player depending on which[b] Sparks[/b] they have available to them, and the rarity of the [b]Sparks[/b]. Often the decisions will be made based on what kind of loadout they are attempting to achieve or try. 

Deciding how much [b]Potential[/b] an item starts with will be something we keep a close eye on as we imagine it will require significant balancing during testing. 
[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/006ae5f0e11343fad13e84fb1e8b0b238b708457.jpg"][/img][/p][p]So we have equipment with base modifiers, bonus modifiers, and [b]Potential[/b] to add [b]Spark[/b] modifiers. The latter two of these are affected by player chosen progression in the way of [b]Facilities [/b]granting bonuses to every player throughout the season.Something to note here is how we plan to incorporate these bonuses into the game, and that is having any bonus only apply to new items created from [b]Artifractal Cores[/b] while the [b]Facilities[/b] are operational. Your old equipment remains the same, but if a Rifle Research [b]Facility,[/b] or Ship Hull Factory [b]Facility [/b]is built, that may be the ideal time to upgrade your loadout with new pieces. You’re going to want to take advantage of the tools and bonuses available to you while they last… the Void is always looking to consume and once a facility has been destroyed, it may be some time before it’s operational again. 
This is a way for us to allow player base power to increase with progress in a social, seasonal way, while also giving players the freedom and agency to upgrade their own equipment as they see fit. 

A fun bonus with the way [b]Facility[/b] upgrades affect player items is that a player joining later in the season won’t have to start at the very beginning. Every piece of equipment created from an [b]Artifractal Core[/b] will benefit from the current state and highest possible modifiers, allowing them to quickly catch up to the current power of players later in the season.

We believe this will provide enough variation to allow players to create a wide variety of loadouts with enough random elements sprinkled on top to really capitalize on some lucky bonus modifier and[b] Spark Potential[/b] rolls.   We’ll be constantly watching how players choose to play and listening to all feedback on these systems. So prepare yourself, especially if you intend on joining us in the early stages of testing. It’s going to be a wild ride with gameplay that may never be experienced again in later seasons as we hone the design of these systems.   [/p]

notes.title: Monthly Development Update - May 2025
notes.content:
We covered all fronts this month at Warped Games, from game dev to marketing to backend infrastructure. One of the biggest wins was the momentum we’ve seen on our Steam page. We’ve spent the past six months consistently updating it with new content, visuals, and community posts. That kind of work doesn’t pay off immediately, it takes time, iteration, and a lot of convincing to get people to hit that Wishlist button. But this month, it clicked.

Thanks to a strong marketing push, more eyes are landing on Warped Universe, and more people are deciding it’s worth a spot on their wishlist. What’s even more exciting is that those numbers are now growing organically, players are discovering the game through other Steam pages, features, and community recommendations. That’s hugely rewarding, and we’ll keep building on that visibility with regular updates and gameplay reveals.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/0fc41f40221a09f57c92fc20a4c0879b3aa3bca1.png[/img]
This month we focused heavily on ships, both player and Void. Void ships used to be simple palette-swapped versions of player ships. That’s now completely changed. Our art and design teams worked together to create an entirely new aesthetic for the Void, pulling more from their origin in the lore and pushing them into something far more eerie and distinct. The new models look truly warped and hostile, exactly as they should!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/9dfa4309393c8103a9dbb93468d6c002b363b0e4.jpg[/img]
Player ships got a major upgrade too. We added loads of new cosmetic parts (like sails, tails, tusks, wings, hulls, masks, and auras), and reworked ship materials across all five battlepass tiers. These changes give players much more control over their visual identity in the universe. We also introduced new aura FX and a modular base system for internal ship skeletons to support even more variations in the future.

A lot of time this month went into tightening gameplay systems and combat feedback. Ammo was removed from player weapons to streamline combat, and damage numbers have been added for both player and enemy hits. This alone makes encounters feel more readable and reactive.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/adf4c006f9b7ee20299a36d495bc6a999430a96a.png[/img]
On the backend side, we synced our latest work with Beamable and continued expanding tools and systems for development. Niagara FX scripts and emitters were pushed to handle new skeletal effects, and we laid the groundwork for future mission interactions by building a flexible base to build them on top of.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/8cdc2c173da17d46d3ed071f7cba6ce3c2e2394c.png[/img]
That’s it for this month’s game development update. We’re making Warped Universe deeper, sharper, and more reactive across the board. Thanks for continuing to follow the journey, whether you're here for the lore, the systems, or just to watch the ships explode in style, we’re glad you’re along for the ride.

[b]Wishlist us on Steam if you haven’t already, and let us know what you think in the comments or on Discord![/b]

notes.title: The Living Map of the Warped Universe
notes.content:
[i]"The System Status Map is a direct projection of the state of our sprawling and fragile environment. As the frontier’s pylons are built and stabilized, sector matter and energy is directly reflected in real time here in the center of Nexus Station. Part model, part news broadcast, part mission board. It's the focus of every warp pioneer, these warped particles entangled at a tiny ratio with the chaos out there. It's the pulse - the vital signs of the star system, and thus we must all monitor it closely."[/i]
[b]- Dr Monica Monos[/b]

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

While many parts of Nexus Station help prepare a player for their journey, one in particular shows them where their actions truly matter. That’s the System Status Map, a massive interactive map of the known universe, displaying live data, and real-time player influence.
At the heart of the monitor is the system’s sun. More than just a visual set piece, the star reflects the Balance of Light and Gravity, a global system mechanic that shifts based on collective player behavior. Each mission you complete tips the scales in one direction or the other.
As the balance shifts further in either direction, certain changes in gameplay occur, movement speed, resistances, damage and skills are all affected

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/3bfd9b3f018576f929790d3481657cc793e330ed.jpg[/img]
Every visual marker is interactive, offering mission options, cooperative goals, and strategic alerts. Whether you're soloing a scout mission or teaming up to contain a Void outbreak, your actions feed into this living display, and the monitor updates in real time..

The System Map shows not just where you can go, but why it matters. Players can see:
[list]
[*] Planets - Both completed and in construction
[*] Facilities on planets - Showing how developed or vulnerable they are
[*] Unmapped sectors - Explore mission areas obscured by Void interference
[*] Active void tears - Unstable zones where enemy invasions are occurring
[*] Pylon networks - Vital objectives required to stabilize new regions and expand the system
[*] Residuum Deposits - Collection and Transport missions required to facilitate the construction of Planets
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/9a3d170d37f1d8d8811e5066d69cf14eadc7f8b4.jpg[/img]
Each facility type adds significant benefits and opportunities upon completion that remain as long as the facility is operational. 

Facility upgrades include:
[list]
[*] Farm Facilities - Provide a health bonus to players embarking on missions
[*] Housing Facilities - Adds choice and reduces costs of end of mission rewards
[*] Power Facilities - Increases the rarity of mission rewards
[*] Factory Facilities - Adds the possibility of rolling certain attributes on equipment obtained from Artifractal Cores
[*] Research Facilities - Increase the Potential of any new piece of equipment in that category 
[*] Spaceport Facilities - Required to kick start a new planet once discovered and constructed
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/0c81f5bacdafac2774bdae36918118d0d58871e5.jpg[/img]
Each of these upgrades is improved further as more of each type of facility is completed throughout the system, changing gameplay options significantly from start of season to the end. 

There’s a strange sensation when using the System Monitor: you feel like a miniature piece on a galactic game board. And in some sense, you are. But unlike a traditional game, the board is unfinished, unmapped, and at risk.
This is what makes the SSM feel alive: it doesn't just reflect the state of the game, it is the state of the game.

The System Status Map turns abstract player behavior into visible consequence. It tracks a shared universe, responds to individual decisions, and serves as the connective tissue for strategy, cooperation, and survival.

It’s not just where you get missions. It’s where you see your impact. Every new region you open, every planet that forms, every moment of collapse or recovery... it all echoes on this surface.

notes.title: Your First 60 Minutes In Warped Universe
notes.content:
[i]“Transition into the Warped Universe is not merely geographic, it is existential. Individuals who volunteer for traversal are often driven by complex emotional and psychological motivations that include the desire for redemption, escape, or transformation. Understanding these motivations is crucial for the ongoing development of civilian acclimation protocols, therapeutic interventions, and mission suitability assessments.
As humanity continues to spread into new dimensions, it must also reckon with the psychological cost of leaving Earth behind, not just the world, but the self that belonged to it.”[/i]
[b] - Dr. Elira Senn
 Civilian Wellness Division, Celadon Station[/b]

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/c6f9253e97cc4d9d14b8cdbb1fe1009398566d09.jpg[/img]
So you’ve just stepped through the portal on Celadon Station. The world you knew is far behind, and ahead lies a station held together by ingenuity, stubbornness, and something stranger. Welcome to the Warped Universe.

Let’s take a look at what to expect in your first hour aboard Nexus Station. Whether you’re a veteran of sci-fi adventures or just curious what you’ve signed up for, here’s how your journey begins.
Your first steps on Nexus Station follow a 15-minute introduction through a vision of the recent past, the fall of Embry’s Hope, the first world consumed by the Void.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/d437a83e7c5a7b83cec48038508704ab1689b2a5.jpg[/img]
In this playable prologue, you’ll experience four core game modes:
[list]
[*] Third-person ground combat 
[*] Turn-based ground tactics
[*] Real-time space action
[*] Turn-based space strategy
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/4461ba3b11bb35381a86f88784506534b468f76d.jpg[/img]
You’ll escort fleeing scientists, try out your first skill, clear asteroid paths for evac ships, and dogfight hostile fighters in orbit. As the planet collapses around you, you witness its final moments.

Then, everything goes white.

As your consciousness rethreads itself, your body begins to reassemble, this time by choice. This is where you define who you are in the Warped Universe. Appearance, name, core traits, this is your moment to shape your identity.
You open your own eyes once more to the pristine interior of Nexus Station, and your journey truly begins.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/3bfd9b3f018576f929790d3481657cc793e330ed.jpg[/img]
After a moment introducing yourself on Nexus, you’ll be thrown right back into the action, this time, it’s your choice of what type of mission you play and how you play it. Completing this, you’ll receive your first Artifractal Core, and learn to make your first piece of equipment, then it's back to the mission map to take on another challenge before receiving a Spark and learning how to upgrade your gear. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/006ae5f0e11343fad13e84fb1e8b0b238b708457.jpg[/img]
Next, you’ll be introduced to the two primary ideologies on Nexus Station. The Foundationalists focus on stability, order, and rebuilding what was lost. The Luminaries seek insight, exploration, and the expansion of what’s known in the Warped Universe. You’ll learn how to gain reputation with both of them through mission choices, unlocking rewards, new challenges, and your place in the social fabric of the station.

[h3]Now it’s game on.[/h3]

Your goal in Warped Universe is to rebuild what was lost after a cosmic catastrophe fractured reality itself. As a survivor and explorer arriving through the portal to Nexus Station, you join the effort to reclaim the galaxy from the chaos of the Void.  Along the way, you'll build your strength, uncover ancient truths, and shape the future of this strange new cosmos.
Your main enemies are entities born from the collapse of the old universe, shaped by fear, memory, and instability. These creatures are unpredictable, often terrifying reflections of what was, or what might have been. They will challenge both your combat skills and your understanding of the universe.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/9e67b9f6ddd680926835deea4168e43551c5d84e.jpg[/img]
Victory isn’t determined by a single event, it’s a long-term journey that involves rebuilding habitable planets, securing territory from Void influence, and strengthening your loadout through Sparks and Cores.
In the future, large-scale collaborative goals and factional conflicts may further define what “winning” means.
From here, you’re free to pursue missions at your pace, upgrade your kit, and learn how the balance of Light and Gravity shapes every encounter.
You’ve got a long road ahead, but your first steps? You’ve taken them..

[h3]Welcome to Warped Universe.[/h3]

notes.title: Harnessing Sparks
notes.content:
[p][i]“While the resources known as “Sparks” are not pure enough to propagate a full construction, they are vital to an ECHO material’s build process. Artifractal Core refinement and expression is a complex and hazardous process that is highly automated. After choosing the type of equipment that will be constructed, the operator has limited control over the exact way that the core tech will be expressed. Fortunately, there is always a certain amount of constructive capacity left in the resultant material. In this potentially available space the item can be further fitted with more customized properties, and this is precisely where Spark augmentation completes the creation.”[/i]

[b]- Memprinting Basics by Dr G. Embry[/b]

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Along with Artifractal Cores, Nexite, and battlepass XP, Sparks are one of the end-of-mission rewards available to choose to push your build even further in Warped Universe.
Sparks are the upgrade resource that allows players to enhance and specialize their equipment beyond its base capabilities.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/a3148bcdddc7140fb1342fafe7569ec7e827cf32.jpg"][/img]Each piece of equipment in Warped Universe comes with a modifier called Potential, a measure of how much specialization the item can handle. Each Spark costs a certain amount of Potential to socket. Higher-tier Sparks provide stronger effects but require more Potential to equip.
Once an item’s Potential is fully spent, no further Sparks can be added.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/de975b6a8ff6291bbf65935c2f3e9793f4c155a5.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/d93abb8ab576c95ec29fc954abc1a038ac849d87.jpg"][/img]Sparks come in different types, each offering a specific kind of bonus when placed into a piece of equipment. Some Sparks increase weapon damage or critical chance, while others boost resistances, skill power, or mobility. The combination of Sparks you choose will greatly influence how your loadout performs in both action and turn-based gameplay.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/2e180663c2966ea30f6c8bf74aeb7972dd57a3ff.jpg"][/img]There are currently ten types of Spark, with some providing different bonus modifiers depending on whether it is placed on a weapon or piece of armor. 

[b]Light[/b] - Adds Light damage dice on weapon, or Light resistance on armor
[b]Gravity[/b] - Adds Gravity damage dice on weapon, or Gravity resistance on armor
[b]Armor Piercing[/b] - Adds Armor Piercing damage dice on weapon, or Armor Piercing resistance on armor
[b]Kinetic[/b] - Adds Kinetic damage dice on weapon, or Kinetic resistance on armor
[b]Void[/b] - Adds Void damage dice on weapon, or Void resistance on armor
[b]Power[/b] - Adds a bonus Power modifier
[b]Precision[/b] - Adds a bonus Precision modifier
[b]Psionics[/b] - Adds a bonus Psionics modifier 
[b]Hit Points[/b] - Adds a bonus Health modifier 
[b]Speed[/b] - Improves Attack Speed on weapon, or Movement Speed on armor. 

Each Rarity of Spark rolls a different dice value that consumes Potential, D4 all the way up to D20, with each rarity granting a larger bonus modifier at the risk of expends more of the item’s Potential. 
For example: A Common Gravity Spark will add D4 Gravity damage to a weapon but may use up 1-4 available Potential on that item, while an Epic Gravity Spark will add D12 Gravity damage to a weapon but may use up 1-12 available Potential on that item.
Note: If your item does not have the maximum possible number of Potential a Spark can use, you risk failing to upgrade and destroying the Spark.
For example: An item only has 2 Potential remaining, if you attempt to apply a Common Spark you have a 50% chance to succeed when rolling a 1 or 2, and an equal chance to fail if rolling a 3 or 4.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/c8e6b66f7504e26854629d77a0bb427c7f645765.jpg"][/img]Choosing how to spend Potential is a big part of defining your loadout.
Will you invest heavily in offense for raw damage output?
Split your Potential between resistances and mobility?
Or design highly specialized builds for specific missions, playstyles, or team roles?

Sparks add another layer of customization and choice to Warped Universe, letting you sharpen your strengths, cover your weaknesses, and improve your favorite gear while also giving you the thrill of hoping for those god rolls for stacked gear. 

[/p][h3]Adapt. Optimize. Unleash your Potential.[/h3]

notes.title: Unfolding Artifractals
notes.content:
[i]“There was a time when we thought the entire warped universe was nothing but stray pockets of particle concentration and massive, scattered fields of inert residuum. As our earliest researchers collected and refined residuum into a usable form they encountered rare deposits of more complex amalgamations of matter. These pieces of crystalized power actually caused a great deal of damage to the processing equipment upon their discovery. The internal reflective surfaces are of a varied complexity with an expected increase in energetic potency. We dubbed them Artifractal Cores. Bring me one of those and watch the tech do the rest.”[/i]

[b]- First Techsmith
[/b]
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Along with Sparks, Nexite, and battlepass XP, Artifractal Cores are one of the end of mission rewards available to choose to progress along your journey in Warped Universe. 
Artifractal Cores, or Cores as they are obviously going to be referred to, are the resource allowing players to acquire new equipment.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/f5e339b2a7c51dc8588f81e9f0835559b598386f.jpg[/img]
Artifractal Cores, or simply “Cores”,  are the basic element required for all weapon and gear crafting in Warped Universe. Since all specialization and stat boosting will be carried out by gear rather than a standard character level-up mechanic, Cores are the foundation and framework of any player loadout. From tanky brawler sets to fast and accurate pieces, (or any combinations in between) the gear built at an Artifractal Core table will provide the player a vast combination of strengths and strategies.
Cores can be obtained in six rarities, common, uncommon, rare, epic, legendary and Warped. The power of any given core is easily predicted by the complexity of its shape.
After receiving a Core, the player must take it to the Artifractal Core table in Nexus Station and choose the equipment you want or need at the time. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/42cbcdfa5ce4f5d8495f54754428e1a577fbc46f.jpg[/img]
When you use a Core table, you’ll be faced with a few choices. First you select whether you want equipment for your ground character or your space ship, armor or weapon, then specifically which piece you want to receive for each loadout. 
You may want a new ship hull for example, go to the table, select ship, then hull, choose your core rarity and hope for the best. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/41128460ffbe74051e75cfc18b02d474b678efaf.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/90ce3f0e65d3c0a37df286de17bc575a99b68204.jpg[/img]
Each piece of equipment comes with its own appearance and base modifiers that will remain the same regardless of Core rarity. There will be equipment with modifiers weighted in all directions, ensuring you have the ability to create multiple loadouts for any scenario.
The benefit of a higher Core rarity is the significant number of desirable bonus modifiers on a piece of equipment. These stat types are randomized from the list of upgrades available from Planet Facility unlocks. 

Modifiers in Warped Universe currently include:

[b]Power[/b] - Reducing weapon recoil and increasing critical strike damage.
[b]Precision[/b] - Increasing accuracy and critical strike chance.
[b]Psionics[/b] - Used to increase skill usage in the form of cool down reduction, skill range, and AoE size.
[b]Health[/b]- Increasing base health points.
[b]Speed[/b] - Increasing movement speed, by percentage in action modes and tiles moved in turn-based.
[b]Dodge[/b] - Decreases the possibility of being hit.
[b]Resists[/b] - Reduces damage received. Comes in the form of armor piercing, kinetic, light, gravity, and void.
[b]Additional Damage Dice[/b] - Increases damage done, and potentially varying the damage types you deal.
[b]Potential[/b] - The resource players spend to further upgrade their equipment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/8cde12d16b68b1de649ef5f32b9dc88b6eee05c2.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/0e38b69b8df8d90e43e3e27431d0e6d77ae9f02a.jpg[/img]
Cores also serve a secondary purpose, allowing players to reset upgrade potential on a piece of equipment, but we’ll get into that later.

The Artifractal Core system provides an opportunity for the player to stay connected to their in-game character regardless of how they want to change or accentuate their playstyle. It provides a frictionless and interesting way to min-max their loadout without abandoning any previous progress. 

Customize your experience, choose your pace, and as always… 

[h3]Play Your Way[/h3]

notes.title: The Constant Conflict
notes.content:
[i]"The endless challenges of propagating a secure population include the construction and maintenance of strange, technically wondrous feats of engineering while beset by a ceaseless tide of invasion. After a time, one yearns for the drudgery of monotonous tasks when the spectre of destruction lurks around every corner. But just as we strive for balance in the universal forces, we must also balance our efforts between the impressive and the inane. The perils are seemingly insurmountable, but the rewards defy imagination. We do what we do not only for the bounty of victory, but also because it is the right thing to do."[/i]
[b]- Orin[/b]

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

At its core, Warped Universe is a battle for creation and survival faced with the constant threat of annihilation. The remnants of a shattered civilization drift over silent distances, caught between the fluctuating forces of Light and Gravity. Players travel to the ruins of this universe, re-shaping its fate through strategic exploration, planetary construction, and high intensity battles.
Missions run the full gamut between complex infiltrations of construction areas on the untamed frontier to simple data collection goals in sparsely infested farmlands. Regardless of the setting and threat, each excursion into the young system’s environments brings a variety of challenges and strategies. Players can always choose a threat level and pace that appeals to their gaming senses.
Our conflict extends beyond simple good versus evil. It’s a struggle of balance, where every action shifts the cosmic scales. Whether you embrace the speed and precision of Light or the raw control and power of Gravity, your choices will influence the battlefield and the universe itself.
Shifting Balance

In Warped Universe the choices players make, and the missions they take have an ever changing effect on the state of the seasons system and gameplay. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/0bbeac853a87ece348b0440c5543f48c71c6ae39.jpg[/img]
The star in the center of the map will show the current balance of Gravity and Light, the effects of which include changing movement speed, jump distance, how skills function, damage, resistances, and more. In the most extreme cases of imbalance, Void enemies will even receive a hefty damage buff. It’ll be up to players to decide whether they want to keep the balance or push it to one side or the other. You may want high gravity to take advantage of a certain loadout and skills, while others may prefer light or to pull things back to the center. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/f7f2413e08c551bf00dc26cbfdaf11c0e31ba570.jpg[/img]
The way in which players direct the balance will come in the form of completing missions assigned to either the Luminaries or Foundationalists. Farms, Housing, and Factory missions push balance towards gravity, while Power, Research, and Space Port missions lean towards the Light. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/04e11fbfa8e1f8e75a667385acfe3390f17b0e35.jpg[/img]
These of course aren't the only mission types you’ll find on the System Map. There are also Explore missions, which are needed to open up the map to find new potential resources. In Pylon missions, players build and defend a network of pylons responsible for creating a safe zone required to begin mining resources or to build a new planet. Residuum missions are escort missions retrieving and transporting Residuum back to Nexus Station. Finally there are the Void Tear missions. Void Tears are a constant threat in the Warped Universe. If a Void Tear isn't closed in time, it can destroy a facility and set back all of the progress made by players. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/f395f9d50f7f0f1e831dde46533ae248fb241c59.jpg[/img]
It will be up to you and the other inhabitants of Warped Universe to decide how much gets explored, which facilities are built, and what is saved. 
[h3]
The Choice is Yours.[/h3]

notes.title: At The Heart Of It All: Nexus Station
notes.content:
[i]“You’re going to need something familiar. Something they can understand. Humans interact with reality in a very concrete way or they get disturbed. They will reject what’s right in front of them if it doesn’t fit their frame of reference. The needs of the civilization should be visible at all times in a clear, distinct way. As far as manifesting matter – they will want to see it fabricated, even if it is they, themselves, who are bringing it into existence.”[/i]
[b]Professor Givens Embry[/b]

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

During our latest Warped Talk Q+A, lead game developer and Warped Games President Scott Brown took us on a tour of the immense social hub and heart of the Warped Universe, Nexus Station. 
Acting as the beating heart of this new civilization tasked with building the Warped Universe, the Nexus Station will provide a space where players can gather, strategize, and take a breath from the destructive forces of the Void.
The Nexus is where players will customize their Echo, receive and upgrade equipment, and choose their missions before departing.

While many areas of the Nexus are still under development, what we now have is almost everything required to experience Warped Universe in it's earliest iteration. 

Upon exiting the portal, the first thing a player will experience is the complex simplicity of the interactive System Map. A real time representation of the current state of the Seasonal System, a hex grid map revealing the current areas available to explore a vast pylon system, retrieve vital Residuum necessary to build new planets and facilities, and seal void tears before they can rip the sector to shreds, and more.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/43d574feaff10bc81d469cf76ff44f86fbe00ba1.jpg[/img]

Underneath the System Map you’ll see the Planet Printhead, a matter fabrication engine of unimaginable power that takes Residuum collected on missions and transmutes it using the warped particle to create planets to expand the Universe.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/a4b8b604ee590b64210a9500d3ff2f8c17db91eb.jpg[/img]

Upon completing missions you’ll receive rewards of your choosing, it may be an Artifractal Core used to receive new equipment, Sparks to upgrade equipment, Nexite which serves as the in-game currency needed to facilitate equipment purchases and upgrades, and/or experience to expedite Battlepass progress. Players will utilize these rewards at various construction tables around the Nexus.
We'll go into more detail on the functions of these in a future update.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/249e5edf047d6fe558152277390278b4e1f8a4db.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/006ae5f0e11343fad13e84fb1e8b0b238b708457.jpg[/img]

Exclusive Battlepass cosmetics will have their own display area within the Nexus where you can see the graphically stunning gear available to those with the gall to grind it out.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/d8d0a4fa0f015d555fd567d5a00ab94f3269c880.jpg[/img]

And once you’ve fitted yourself with your upgraded equipment, and unlocked some cosmetics, you’ll want to customize your appearance to your liking. Visual Customization stations are located around the Nexus so you’ll never have to travel too far to change things up. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/5b928721417cb3e47c137e3ddfe919be17267222.jpg[/img]

notes.title: The Space Game
notes.content:
"Time can move slower out there, if you want. This reality is not exactly the same as what we’re used to back home. I prefer to watch closely and plan my moves. Trouble is, in that mode of consciousness the void has time to plan its moves as well. Think about what they might do. You should know their strategies. They are likely your own. Outmaneuver, outgun, and for Oracle’s sake use cover. You won’t be covering as much ground as other missions, but it may feel like it.”
-Orin

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[h2]Space Combat in Warped Universe[/h2]
Once again, the choice is yours. In the interplanetary battlefield, movement takes place over vast distances rather than tight confines. Sweeping maneuvers may be useful but must always be purposeful. 

[h3]Think Fast, Act Faster[/h3]
In action space combat, one is always both predator and prey. Focus on a single target and your flank could be fully exposed. Prioritizing defensive maneuvers may sacrifice opportunities that would otherwise bring about a swift resolution. Players must be both pilot and navigator if they want to return to Nexus Station in triumph. Those excelling in rapid reactions will enjoy everything that action space combat has to offer.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/d235be4b809175b0420d18c6727a01cfe9c6e21d.jpg[/img]
[h3]Limited Turns Require Meaningful Choices[/h3]
Turn-based space combat takes tactical vision and careful consideration. Time is no longer the enemy, rather the limited capabilities of rapid directional changes and high speed propulsion. 

Your enemy will take advantage of the same dilated time mechanic to actively thwart your efforts at every turn. Taking place on a hexagonally divided map, three dimensional space is visualized on a single plane. A considered approach to combat on such a playing field will be a vital component of the player’s strategy, and a major determinant of success.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45514248/56854031ee627d31cf950be9d9d4d36b9b9161a7.jpg[/img]
Choice is the name of the game. Whether it’s turn-based or third-person action, you get to choose how you face each challenge in the Warped Universe.

[h3]Shared Systems, Unique Experiences[/h3]
No matter how you play, the core mechanics remain consistent. Equipment loadouts, upgrades, and abilities function across both modes, allowing you to seamlessly switch between styles depending on the mission or your preferred playstyle.
[h2]
The Choice is Yours[/h2]

notes.title: The Ground Game
notes.content:
“Listen up Freshprint. You’re gonna be in a big place without much help. The structures are stable but have lots of nooks and crannies for these beetle boys to crawl out of. You gotta get in and get out. Hit your objectives and get to the extraction point. They’ll usually be in groups but don’t think one of those bastards won’t sit and watch his buddies evaporate while he waits patiently for you to let your guard down. In, out. Kapiche?”
-Vanir

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[h2][b]Ground Combat in Warped Universe[/b][/h2]
Choice is the name of the game. Turn-based or action, on the ground or in space. You get to choose how you face each challenge in the Warped Universe.
Whether you're engaging in methodical, strategic encounters through turn-based combat or diving into the chaos of real-time action, the battlefield is yours to control. But each mode brings its own strengths and challenges.

[h3][b]Two Ways to Fight[/b][/h3]
In turn-based, every move counts, positioning, resource management, and ability combinations determine the outcome of each battle. Take the time to analyze enemy positioning, set up combos, and maximize your advantage. How you deal with environmental hazards and cover will play a key role in ensuring you complete your objectives. 

In action gameplay, however, there are no turns, no waiting, just pure movement and instinct. Battles are fast, fluid, and driven by player skill. If you can’t sneak up on your foes to take advantage of the first move, you’ll have to dodge as much incoming fire as you can to survive. Momentum is your greatest weapon.

[h3][b]Shared Systems, Unique Experiences[/b][/h3]
No matter how you play, the core mechanics remain consistent. Equipment loadouts, upgrades, and abilities function across both modes, allowing you to seamlessly switch between styles depending on the mission or your preferred playstyle.


[b]The Choice is Yours [/b]
